html:
SMTO-POL-0008 — The situation changed after you confirmed going ahead

GUID: e6a723f7-03ec-44bc-be26-ac48869ae719
Slug: resource-unsafe-confirmation-stale
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • You confirmed going ahead with a blocked task, but the earlier job's situation changed before SMTO could use your answer. SMTO won't apply an old answer to a new situation, so nothing has run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and read the recovery card again, including its 'Blocking job:' line. The card now shows the earlier job's latest state, and any new decision must match it.
  2. Select Wait until the job state changes on the task's recovery card if the earlier job might still be working. SMTO continues by itself once that job is done. Waiting lets the earlier job finish first, so the two never change the same thing at once.
  3. Select Resolve forcefully by terminating job only if you are sure the earlier job is no longer needed. The button is greyed out when SMTO can't stop it safely. Stopping the earlier job frees what your task needs without two jobs working on it together.

What success looks like

  • The recovery card accepts your new choice and shows 'Job state updated.' or 'Blocking job claims restored.'

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend your earlier answer; it belongs to a situation that no longer exists.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Recovery authority could not accept or consume the override challenge because its binding (run, candidate, blocker revision, resource scope) no longer matches the current recovery state, or the challenge was already used.

What this means

  • Recovery authority could not consume the confirmation against its current binding, so a prior confirmation cannot authorize the changed state. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Recovery authority could not consume the confirmation against its current binding, so a prior confirmation cannot authorize the changed state.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh the blocker revision and pending recovery challenge; compare them with the confirmation being submitted.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the run's resource-reconciliation state, then request a new override challenge and submit it against the current blocker_revision, or use the wait/reset actions the projection now enables. A previously accepted challenge cannot authorize a changed binding.
  • Refresh the resource state and review a fresh confirmation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A new confirmation matches the current recovery state at the point it is consumed.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
